title: Portable Driver Triage — scope profile
description: Formal shape of a YAML file under scope_profiles/. Each profile declares a vulnerability-class hunt: what the L1 pipeline looks for, how it ranks hits, what deep-analysis focus it hands to L3, and which handler-side checks the L3 validation-gap detector should expect.

name.description: Stable identifier. Must equal the filename stem (<name>.yaml). Appears verbatim in index.jsonl at run.scope_profile and in scope_matches[].scope.

short_name.description: Short tag used as <scope-short> in run_id (see schemas/index_row.schema.json). ≤ 10 chars, lowercase alphanumeric only.

severity_prior.description: Operator's expectation when the profile fires. Informs severity_in_scope in AI findings but does not constrain it.

must_have_one.description: GATE. The profile does not fire for a driver unless it imports at least one of these. Keeps the index clean of noise.

weight_each.description: Each hit adds rank_weights.dangerous_imports to the overall rank. Empty array is valid.

methods_of_interest.description: IOCTL dispatch methods. Convention: list worst-first (METHOD_NEITHER usually first).

ioctl_patterns.description: Python-regex patterns applied to normalized IOCTL strings in the form 0xHHHHHHHH, lowercase hex. Empty array is valid when the profile does not restrict by IOCTL range.

device_name_patterns.description: Python-regex patterns applied to \\Device\\... names found in L1. Empty array is valid when device names are weak signal for this class (e.g., process-token-manipulation).

strings_of_interest.description: Substrings for scope-level string matching (on top of what L1 already extracts into interesting_strings). Case-insensitive, matched against both ASCII and UTF-16LE decodes.

device_classes_of_interest.description: Subset of the closed device_classes vocabulary (see schemas/index_row.schema.json and refs/device_classes.yaml). Must stay in sync with that enum — if a new class is added there, bump this file too.

clone_cves.description: CVEs whose reference snippets, if matched by L3 clone-detection, bump the rank sharply. Empty array is valid — not every class has indexed CVEs (e.g., hid-input-control, smm-smi).

rank_weights.description: Multipliers used by the additive ranking formula. All seven keys required. Negative weights are not allowed — a profile cannot penalize a signal. See docs/ranking.md for the exact formula.

oneOf.description: Bare selector name. See docs/l3_focus_selectors.md for the vocabulary and which selectors are generic (interpreted by the pipeline core) versus profile-specific (require dedicated L3 code).
Parameterized selector of the form {selector_name: parameter_reference}. The parameter typically names another top-level field on this profile (e.g., taint_sinks).

l3_focus.description: Hints the L3 function gate uses to decide which handlers get full pseudo-C decompilation. Mix of generic selectors (interpreted by the pipeline) and profile-specific heuristics (require dedicated L3 code). Unimplemented heuristics degrade gracefully — the pipeline runs the generic selectors and logs the unimplemented ones in the bundle's summary.md.

taint_sinks.description: Sinks the L3 taint pass must reach from a user-controlled source for the handler to be reported as confirmed-primitive. Symbol names as they appear in the import table or (for intrinsics) in the mnemonic scan.

validation_expected.description: Named checks the handler should perform on user input before granting the capability. Vocabulary is documented in docs/validation_checks.md; entries not backed by an L3 detector are silently ignored (reported in summary.md as 'detector not implemented').
